minutes.headline: Building panel unveils ~$15M plan to move schools into Ritter, restore Town Hall; Turkey Hill's fate left open
minutes.summary: The Municipal Building Design Committee presented its plan to relocate school offices into the former Ritter library building, restore Town Hall as a community meeting house, and build a new administrative annex, while leaving Turkey Hill's future to a later school committee decision tied to an ongoing facilities study. The board also discussed the statewide elimination of the MCAS graduation requirement, weighed whether to adopt a district cell phone policy (referring it to school advisory councils), and reviewed calendar options for the December 2025 holiday break. Only the prior minutes and adjournment were formally voted on; other matters were discussion, reports, or informal direction.

votes.motion: Motion to approve the regular session minutes of October 2, 2024.

budget_items.what_was_said: The committee reviewed warrants covering November 5 to November 15; no line-item transfers or donations were reported for the period.
The select board approved ARPA funding for two capital-plan items: a truck and plow, and Middle/High School safety window film.
The design committee chair estimated the combined cost of renovating Town Hall and the Ritter building and building a new town hall annex.
The chair said renovation costs per square foot have risen sharply in recent years, making renovation nearly as expensive as new construction.
Beardmore reported the interim town manager told the select board that initial health insurance quotes for the coming year were higher than the estimate used last year.
Beardmore cited the increase in the average tax bill from last year to this year and warned the building plan would add further cost on top of it.

budget_items.topic: New town hall addition, cost formula
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair walked through a rough per-square-foot formula for the new town hall addition based on added square footage.
Beardmore referenced the approximate added cost per household from a prior override vote, though he said he was not certain of the exact figure.

budget_items.topic: Busing costs vs. the levy cap
budget_items.what_was_said: Scullbrini said busing cost increases are outpacing the property tax levy cap, creating a structural budget gap, and urged the legislative delegation to help fix it.
Brazowski reported that Wellesley maintains a substantial special education stabilization fund and sometimes uses it to prepay special education tuition in advance.

Brazowski reported from the MASC conference that school committees are required by law to formally vote to accept all grants and donations, including entitlement grants, which Lunenburg does not currently do.
Beardmore said he will recommend removing ARPA-funded items, such as the truck/plow and window film, from the capital plan since they already have a funding source.

budget_items.topic: Community Preservation Act funding for affordable housing
budget_items.what_was_said: Scullbrini said the budget task force is researching whether Lunenburg could meet the CPA's affordable-housing spending requirement before recommending a CPA warrant article for spring town meeting.

transfers.outcome: discussed only - none reported this period

decisions.decision: Cell phone policy development will be referred to each school's advisory council to gather stakeholder input before any districtwide policy is drafted.
Beardmore will email each state legislator individually, and the legislative delegation will become a standing agenda item until town meeting.
Beardmore will recommend the capital planning committee remove ARPA-funded items (the truck/plow and window film) from the capital plan, with no objection raised.
Committee members agreed to send their individual master-planning priority survey responses to the superintendent by December 2 for submission to the master planning committee.

what_happened.line: A building design committee proposed moving school offices into the former Ritter library and restoring Town Hall as a meeting space, leaving Turkey Hill's future to a later decision tied to a facilities study.
A member said rising busing costs are outpacing the property tax levy cap, calling it a structural gap and asking the legislative delegation for help.
The board referred development of a districtwide cell phone policy to each school's advisory council rather than drafting one centrally.
The legislative delegation will become a standing agenda item until town meeting, with a member emailing individual state legislators.
Only the prior meeting's minutes and the adjournment were put to a formal vote; the building plan, MCAS, phone policy and calendar were discussion or referral only.

why_it_matters: The building plan was discussed alongside a reported rise in the average tax bill, and any construction cost that reaches a town vote would come on top of that.
A busing-cost gap described as outrunning the levy cap points to a budget pressure that a town vote alone cannot close without a legislative change.
A cell phone policy will now be shaped school by school through advisory councils rather than set once for the district, so any rules may differ by building until that work concludes.
